html:
The Bamana Empire, also called the kingdom of Ségou, was a state of the Bambara people on the middle Niger River, in what is now Mali. The map shows it as Segu from 1715 to 1800.

It was founded around 1712 by Biton Coulibaly, who turned a young men's association into a standing army. Its soldiers, many of them captives, raided widely, and the kingdom sold captives into the slave trade in exchange for guns and goods. In 1766 a new line, the Diarra (Ngolo Diarra and his heirs), took the throne.

At its height Ségou controlled the Niger from near Bamako to Timbuktu and its trading cities, such as Djenné. Its rulers kept the Bambara religion while Muslim traders lived and worked in its towns. The Scottish explorer Mungo Park reached Ségou in 1796.

A related Bambara kingdom, Kaarta, lay to the west and was often at war with it. In 1861 the Muslim leader Umar Tall conquered Ségou and made it part of his Toucouleur Empire.
